messages:
mia: Heads up — I'm bringing up hf/aster-13b-open on int4 for a quick smoke and seeing token-level shadowing in long contexts >2048.

mia: Repro (super short):
```python
model = load_model('hf/aster-13b-open', dtype='int4', quant_config={'mode':'perchannel','sym':True})
out = model.generate(tokenizer.encode(prompt), max_new_tokens=512)
```

mia: Sample failure: prompt mentions 'protocol X' and model repeats an earlier subword instead of generating related entity; weird duplicates across runs.

tom: can you paste a tiny golden input/output pair?

mia: sure — input: "Compare protocol X vs Y in long thread"
output-int4: "Compare protocol X vs protocol X in long thread"
output-fp16: "Compare protocol X vs Y in long thread"

arya: my first guess is vocab id offsets. Did the tokenizer or embedding matrix get an extra sentinel row during conversion?

mia: tokenizer.vocab_size==51200 but embedding matrix shape is (51201, 4096). there is a mysterious row at index 0 that looks like a pad/bos sentinel.

max: that off-by-one is a red flag. When we quantize, int4 can cause aliasing: rows that differ slightly in float end up colliding to same 4-bit bucket. Have you checked for identical rows after quant?

mia: eyeballed some rows — row 0 and row 256 look eerily similar post-quant.

deploy-bot: CI: model-smoke-int4 failed — perplexity delta +8.2 on lm_eval-subset.

ravi: another angle: Aster uses per-head rotary frequencies (headwise). Our loader defaults to global rotary_scale. If rotary axes are misapplied after conversion, long-term token mixing gets corrupted. Try toggling rotary mapping: headwise vs global.

mia: switched to headwise rotary mapping (rotary.set_param(mode='headwise')) — continuity improved but embedding cosine drift still high.

arya: do a quick embed drift check: cosine(float16_embed, int4_embed) on a 32-example few-shot set. If mean < 0.95 it's bad.

mia: ran it: mean cosine = 0.72. baseline float16->float16 = 0.998.

max: ugh. That suggests quantization or vocab remap issues, not just rotary. Two quick experiments: 1) rerun quant with per-channel symmetric and larger calibration set (~10k tokens) 2) try remapping tokenizer ids to drop the sentinel rather than deleting rows in embeddings.

mia: thinking of a temporary hack: shift tokenizer ids by -1 and drop the embedding row 0. risky but fast to test.

arya: don't mutate ids without a remap table. Create explicit mapping file: old->new. That keeps provenance and is reversible. Also add a test for kvcache alignment — an off-by-one there will manifest only in long contexts.

max: another gotcha I ran into: numpy endianness / dtype mismatches when saving intermediate arrays. If model.bin was saved with wrong dtype ordering, quant bins can be off. checksum the raw float table before quant and after export.

mia: good call. I'll diff checksums. Also attaching a tiny log snippet here for perf numbers across context lengths:
```
context   perplexity_fp16   perplexity_int4
512       12.3             13.1
1024      13.0             16.8
2048      14.2             22.5
```

ravi: that scale-up at 2048 aligns with rotary/KV misalignment. When rotary frequencies are headwise but applied globally, attention mixing breaks as sequence length grows.

mia: quick patch plan: 1) run per-channel symmetric quant (10k calib) 2) export with explicit tokenizer remap table to drop sentinel 3) enable headwise rotary mapping 4) validate embedding cosine >0.95 and lm_eval delta <+1.

ci-bot: FYI — if this model is used in any prod route please tag #eng-oncall and create an incident if errors >0.5%/min.

max: also add an integration test that compares decode outputs between fp16 baseline and int4 with tolerances (exact top-k match for first 32 tokens or textual diff score).

mia: will run the three-step patch now, post results in this thread. thanks for triage tips. :v:
